title: Pin the client mirrors of table-core constants to the Rust source
body:
## Summary
Seven client copies of table-core constants are hand-maintained and no test compares them with Rust; only mandate.rs reasons are pinned.

## Description
apps/desktop/client/src/lib/format.ts:8 copies Currency::exponent (crates/table-core/src/money.rs:26) for 16 currencies; lib/marketWatch.ts:10-11 copies MAX_MARKET_CHECKS_DAY / MAX_WATCHED_ITEMS (crates/table-core/src/mandate.rs:96,98) and :16 the market_product_valid bound (crates/table-core/src/market.rs:28); mock/rescue.ts:70-71 copies RESCUE_WATCH_MAX / RESCUE_WATCH_READS_DAY (crates/table-core/src/rescue.rs:232,235); mock/forecast.ts:22 copies CORROBORATION_SECS (crates/table-core/src/deal.rs:191). lib/mandateRules.test.ts:17 already shows the house pattern (read the Rust file, strip comments, compare). Fixed: one vitest that reads the named Rust constants and asserts each client copy (registry invariant-placement / build-time-evaluation-of-cross-value-invariants: a table maintained by hand gets a checker that reads the ground truth).

## Flow
- add apps/desktop/client/src/lib/coreConstants.test.ts reading money.rs, mandate.rs, market.rs, rescue.rs, deal.rs (comments stripped)
- assert EXPONENT, MAX_MARKET_CHECKS_DAY, MAX_WATCHED_ITEMS, productValid bound, RESCUE_WATCH_MAX, RESCUE_WATCH_READS_DAY, CORROBORATION_SECS
- seed: change one Rust value in a scratch copy and watch the test go red

## Expected impact
A Rust change to an exponent or allowance turns the client suite red instead of letting the editor and mock show other numbers than the wallet enforces. Nothing breaks; test only.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - client mirrors cannot drift from table-core silently
Before: 7 mirrored constants, 0 pinned (grep table-core/src in client tests: only mandate.rs)
After: 7 of 7 pinned (predicted)
Method: simulation - the fix lives in apps/desktop/client (outside this round); counted the mirrors by grep
Result: better
Gate: none
impact: A Rust change to an exponent or allowance turns the client suite red instead of letting the editor and mock show other numbers than the wallet enforces. Nothing breaks; test only.
instrument: new vitest lib/coreConstants.test.ts reading the Rust consts; seeded red by editing one value

title: marketWatch.ts hand-copies pre_capture instead of the generated PRE_CAPTURE set
body:
## Summary
lib/marketWatch.ts:28 lists the eight pre-capture states by hand for the buyer side of market_watch_open, while bindings/dealStates.ts exports PRE_CAPTURE generated from DealState::pre_capture.

## Description
market_watch_open (crates/table-core/src/market_watch.rs:32) is `Side::Buyer => state.pre_capture()`. The client mirror BUYER_OPEN (apps/desktop/client/src/lib/marketWatch.ts:28) is a literal set of 8 states. bindings/dealStates.ts:9 is generated from the same predicate (crates/table-client/src/deal_states.rs:17) and is now pinned to the transition graph (commit 087b338). Fixed: BUYER_OPEN = PRE_CAPTURE.

## Flow
- replace the literal BUYER_OPEN with an import of PRE_CAPTURE from @bindings/dealStates
- run vitest src/lib/marketWatch.test.ts

## Expected impact
A future pre-capture state is watched on the client exactly when Rust watches it. Nothing else changes.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one definition of the buyer watch window
Before: 2 definitions (Rust predicate + client literal of 8)
After: 1 (generated set)
Method: simulation - out-of-scope file; set equality checked by eye against bindings/dealStates.ts:9
Result: better
Gate: none
impact: A future pre-capture state is watched on the client exactly when Rust watches it. Nothing else changes.
instrument: vitest src/lib/marketWatch.test.ts plus a one-line assertion that BUYER_OPEN === PRE_CAPTURE

title: Export the exposure fold state sets so the mock stops copying them
body:
## Summary
mock/exposure.ts:16-18 hand-copies exposure.rs committed_state and paid_state; neither is a DealState predicate, so the generated dealStates bindings cannot carry them.

## Description
crates/table-core/src/exposure.rs:72-90 defines committed_state (4 states) and paid_state (6 states, UNCONFIRMED counted as spent) as private fns. The browser mock (apps/desktop/client/src/mock/exposure.ts:16,18) repeats both as literal sets; a state added to either Rust list leaves the mock folding money differently. Fixed: make them DealState::is_committed / is_paid (table-core), add two rows to crates/table-client/src/deal_states.rs SETS, regenerate bindings/dealStates.ts, import in the mock.

## Flow
- add pub const fn DealState::is_committed / is_paid in crates/table-core/src/deal.rs; exposure.rs calls them
- add COMMITTED / PAID rows to table-client deal_states.rs SETS; cargo run -p table-client --bin generate-bindings
- mock/exposure.ts imports COMMITTED / PAID from @bindings/dealStates
- gates: cargo test -p table-core -p table-client; vitest src/mock/exposure.test.ts

## Expected impact
The mock exposure page and the wallet count held/committed/paid money from one list. Touches a shared generated surface (bindings/), hence B.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - exposure state sets have one definition
Before: 2 definitions of each of 2 sets (Rust private fns + mock literals)
After: 1 each, generated
Method: simulation - spans table-core, table-client, bindings and the mock
Result: better
Gate: none
impact: The mock exposure page and the wallet count held/committed/paid money from one list. Touches a shared generated surface (bindings/), hence B.
instrument: table-client bindings test (every_set_lists_exactly_the_states_its_predicate_keeps) covers the new rows; vitest mock/exposure.test.ts

title: Shield copy names a pause line one minor unit above the real 1.4x rule
body:
## Summary
modules/shield/matrix.ts:105,186 draws and words the pause line as Math.round(median * 1.4); Rust holds when price * 10 > median * 14, whose exact line is floor(median * 1.4).

## Description
MarketRef::over_forty_percent (crates/table-core/src/market.rs:443) is strict integer arithmetic. The client says "Above <flag> the shield pauses the payment" with flag = Math.round(m.median.minor * 1.4) (apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/modules/shield/matrix.ts:105-107). When 1.4 x median has a fraction >= .5 the rounding goes up: median 202 -> flag 283, but Rust already holds 283 (2830 > 2828), so the copy says a price the shield pauses is fine. Fixed: flag = Math.floor(m.median.minor * 14 / 10) (integer, no float), also in bandGeometry :186 and the console Checks.tsx:83 (sibling-owned this wave).

## Flow
- median.minor = 202, unit price 283
- Rust: over_forty_percent(283) = true -> HOLD
- client copy: "Above 2.83 the shield pauses" -> 2.83 reads as allowed

## Expected impact
The owner reads the true threshold. Off by one minor unit, on 3 of every 5 medians (fraction .6 or .8).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the stated pause line equals the enforced one
Before: median 202: copy line 283, enforced line 282 (3 of 5 medians disagree by 1 minor unit)
After: floor(14m/10): agree on every median
Method: simulation - walked medians 201-205 under both formulas; fix is in client files outside this round
Result: better
Gate: none
impact: The owner reads the true threshold. Off by one minor unit, on 3 of every 5 medians (fraction .6 or .8).
instrument: vitest over medians 1..1000: price floor(14m/10)+1 is over, floor(14m/10) is not, and the copy flag equals floor(14m/10)

title: RETRY_AFTER_FIX 24 h boundary differs between Rust (<=) and the client (<)
body:
## Summary
check_lever refuses a retry when PayPal's own retry is <= 86400 s away; the client grid turns it off only when < 86400 s away; acceptance R1 says "under 24 h".

## Description
crates/table-core/src/rescue.rs:46 `at.saturating_sub(now) <= 86400`; apps/desktop/client/src/windows/main/modules/rescue/model.ts:78 `deadline - now < DAY`. At exactly 24 h the client shows the lever on and the wallet refuses it. docs/design/the-table.extract.txt:938 (R1) reads "under 24 h away", which matches the client. The lever is not built yet (validate refuses every lever but the discount, mandate.rs), so nothing moves money today. Decide one boundary: making the client agree with Rust is display-only and fail-closed; making Rust agree with R1 is a policy-loosen and would go to C.

## Flow
- next_retry = now + 86400
- Rust check_lever -> RetryUnavailable
- client cellState -> not "off: retry <24h"

## Expected impact
The owner never sees a lever offered that the wallet would refuse. Display-only on the client side.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one boundary for the R1 retry rule
Before: 2 boundaries (<= in Rust, < in client)
After: 1 (<= in both)
Method: simulation - walked now+86400 through both; client file out of scope
Result: better
Gate: none
impact: The owner never sees a lever offered that the wallet would refuse. Display-only on the client side.
instrument: vitest case in modules/rescue/model.test.ts at deadline = now + 86400 expecting off

title: Mandate validate signs zero money limits that check() can never allow
body:
## Summary
validate() states "a policy check() could never allow is refused at signing", yet it accepts a zero per-deal max_amount, a zero velocity max_total_day and a zero buyer ceiling, each of which refuses every intent.

## Description
crates/table-core/src/mandate.rs validate refuses empty lists and zero counts but not zero money: PerDeal max_amount 0 (check: amount > 0 always, since Terms::amount rejects a zero price, crates/table-core/src/deal.rs:70), Velocity max_total_day 0, and a Band ceiling of 0 for a buy-only mandate. WalletEnvelope::validate (crates/table-core/src/exposure.rs:286) already refuses zero limits ("a wallet limit of zero allows nothing"): the two signing gates disagree. The client mirror lib/mandateRules.ts is pinned to mandate.rs reasons by mandateRules.test.ts, so a new Rust reason needs the mirror, its words and the test in the same change. Policy-tighten; stored mandates carrying a zero would start failing hash()/validate() (fail closed - they already allowed nothing).

## Flow
- owner signs a mandate with per-deal max 0.00
- validate() -> Ok, the mandate is signed and shown as active
- every intent -> clause 3 refusal; the owner learns per intent, not at signing
- fix: validate refuses the three zeros with one new reason; mirror in lib/mandateRules.ts + REASON_WORDS; test in mandate.rs and mandateRules.test.ts

## Expected impact
The owner is told at signing that the rules allow nothing. Could break: any fixture or stored mandate with a zero limit (grep before landing).

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - every never-allowing mandate is refused at signing
Before: 3 zero-money shapes signable that refuse every intent
After: 0
Method: simulation - three shapes walked through check(); fix spans mandate.rs and the client mirror
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence:
crates/table-core/src/mandate.rs:296 // A policy check() could never allow is refused at signing
crates/table-core/src/deal.rs:68-71 qty == 0 || unit_price.minor() == 0 -> InvalidTerms
crates/table-core/src/exposure.rs:286 a wallet limit of zero allows nothing
impact: The owner is told at signing that the rules allow nothing. Could break: any fixture or stored mandate with a zero limit (grep before landing).
instrument: mandate.rs test: each zero shape -> validate() Err with the new reason; mandateRules.test.ts stays green with the mirror updated

title: check_lever, RescueContext and discounted have no caller: delete or wire R1
body:
## Summary
The R1 retry rule (check_lever, RescueContext, discounted and three RescueError variants) is tested but called by nothing; the levers it guards cannot be signed.

## Description
crates/table-core/src/rescue.rs:13-65 holds check_lever (retry refused on REPLAY or within 24 h, capture <= outstanding), RescueContext and discounted. A grep over crates, services and the client finds no caller outside rescue.rs tests; validate refuses every lever but DISCOUNT_THIS_CYCLE (mandate.rs "only the discount this cycle is available"), and the discount path uses propose_discount/check_offer. The code encodes acceptance R1 (docs/design/the-table.extract.txt:938) for levers that are not built. Deleting it is verified dead code (~55 lines + a test) but drops the only executable statement of R1; keeping it leaves a policy that reads as enforced and is not. That is a product call.

## Flow
- grep check_lever|RescueContext|discounted( across crates, services, client -> rescue.rs only
- option A: delete, keep R1 in the design doc
- option B: keep, mark staged-for-the-lever in STATUS.md

## Expected impact
Either the dead surface goes, or it is labelled as staged. Removal breaks no consumer (0 found).

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - no policy code that looks enforced and is not
Before: 3 pub items + 3 error variants, 0 callers
After: A: 0 / B: same code, documented as staged
Method: probe - zero-consumer grep run this round
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: direction
evidence:
grep -rn "check_lever|RescueContext|discounted(" crates services apps --include=*.rs --include=*.ts -> crates/table-core/src/rescue.rs only
crates/table-core/src/mandate.rs only the discount this cycle is available
impact: Either the dead surface goes, or it is labelled as staged. Removal breaks no consumer (0 found).
instrument: none needed for A beyond cargo check --workspace --all-targets; the decision is which option
